content.text: I fixed it, and all 3 visible tests now pass. The only file I changed is `solution/core.py`. The cause was operand order in the binary operations (`ADD`, `SUB`, `MUL`, `DIV`, `MOD`, `EQ`, `LT`, `GT`): the code used `a, b = pop(), pop()`, which put the top of the stack into `a`. Every non-commutative operation therefore ran with its operands reversed. That's why `1 2 LT` returned 0, why `1 0 DIV` divided 0 by 1 instead of raising `VMZeroDivision`, and why the countdown loop's `SUB` produced `1 - x`, so the counter never reached zero and the step limit was hit. Changing the pop to `b, a = pop(), pop()` makes the second-from-top value the left operand. While reading the code I also found that `SWAP` was a no-op: it popped two values and pushed them back in their original order. None of the visible tests use `SWAP`, so I fixed it too; it now exchanges the top two values, and I checked by hand that `1 2 SWAP` gives `[2, 1]`.

While reading the code I also found that `SWAP` was a no-op: it popped two values and pushed them back in their original order. None of the visible tests use `SWAP`, so I fixed it too; it now exchanges the top two values, and I checked by hand that `1 2 SWAP` gives `[2, 1]`.
